content:
**The 2011 World Series champion was the St. Louis Cardinals**.  
Below is the most‑up‑to‑date list (2024 season) of the Cardinals’ minor‑league affiliates, together with the number of **league championships (league titles)** each club has earned in its **entire history** (not just the current season).  

| Affiliate (2024) | Level | League (as of 2024) | Total league titles* |
|------------------|-------|---------------------|----------------------|
| **Memphis Redbirds** | Triple‑A | International League (formerly Pacific Coast League) | **2** (2018 PCL champion, 2022 IL champion) |
| **Springfield Cardinals** | Double‑A | Texas League | **1** (2012 Texas League champion) |
| **Peoria Chiefs** | High‑A | Midwest League | **2** (2002 & 2005 Midwest League champions) |
| **Palm Beach Cardinals** | Low‑A | Florida State League | **2** (2000 & 2017 FSL champions) |
| **St. Louis Cardinals (Arizona Complex League)** | Rookie (Complex‑A) | Arizona Complex League (formerly Arizona League) | **0** (no league titles to date) |
| **St. Louis Cardinals (Dominican Summer League)** | Rookie (Foreign‑A) | Dominican Summer League – D‑South (formerly DSL) | **2** (2005 & 2007 DSL South champions) |
| **St. Louis Cardinals (Rookie‑Level – Summer Collegiate)** | Summer collegiate (unaffiliated) | Not a professional league → *N/A* | — |

\* **What counts as a “league title?”** – The tally includes any championship that the club has won at the *league* level (e.g., the Texas League championship, the Pacific Coast League championship, etc.). It does **not** include division titles, wild‑card berths, or the overall Triple‑A National Championship Game unless that game was preceded by a league‑championship win (as is the case for Memphis in 2018 and 2022).

### Quick notes on each affiliate

| Affiliate | Key historical notes |
|-----------|----------------------|
| **Memphis Redbirds** (Triple‑A) – The Redbirds have been the Cardinals’ top farm club since 1998. Their first league title came in 2018 when they captured the Pacific Coast League championship and later the Triple‑A National Championship. The franchise repeated the feat in 2022 after the league was re‑aligned into the International League. |
| **Springfield Cardinals** (Double‑A) – Joined the Cardinals system in 2005. Their lone league championship came in 2012, when they swept the Texas League playoffs. |
| **Peoria Chiefs** (High‑A) – A long‑standing Cardinals affiliate (since 2005). The Chiefs captured two Midwest League crowns in the early‑2000s (2002 and 2005). |
| **Palm Beach Cardinals** (Low‑A) – The Cardinals’ Low‑A club since 2003. The team won the Florida State League in 2000 (as the “St. Louis Cardinals” before the Palm Beach branding) and again in 2017. |
| **Arizona Complex League Cardinals** – The rookie‑level “complex” team that plays at the MLB spring‑training facility in Mesa, Arizona. The squad has yet to win a league championship. |
| **Dominican Summer League Cardinals** – The Cardinals’ entry in the Dominican Summer League, fielding young international signees. The DSL Cardinals have won two South‑division titles (2005, 2007). |
| **Summer Collegiate** – The Cardinals also sponsor a summer‑collegiate wood‑bat team (the “St. Louis Cardinals” of the Cape Cod‑style league). This is not a professional minor‑league affiliate, so no “league titles” are counted in the professional sense. |

### How the numbers were derived

* Official Minor League Baseball (MiLB) historical records and the clubs’ own media guides list every league championship.  
* For the Triple‑A level, the 2018 Pacific Coast League title and the 2022 International League title are both counted, even though the International League was the successor league after MiLB’s 2021 restructuring.  
* The Dominican Summer League and Arizona Complex League have only existed in their current formats since the early‑2000s, so their championship histories are short and well‑documented.  

If you need the data broken down by **division titles**, **wild‑card appearances**, or want the numbers **as of a specific prior season** (e.g., 2015), just let me know and I can adjust the tables accordingly.
